title: RAW UNREVIEWED: crossed f100v/f77r inscription and prose forms as a directed object-use pair
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. GDT812 records exact dchdy in a f100v botanical inscription and a f77r arch inscription, while exact soral occurs in f100v prose and a f77r inscription. This crossed channel pattern could reflect a stable object or substance paired with a use or property relation, or two unrelated reusable register forms. First obtain independently singular owners for each inscription and a complete reading of both local prose records; current proximity supplies neither. Freeze both exact whole forms and all ZL3b/IT2a/RF1b boundaries before any interpretation. The proposal does not reopen GDT812's rejected cross-page edge packet, does not assign a botanical species, and yields no translated word now. Primary: experiments/yolo/gdt812_additional_page_semantic_bridge/src/CROSS_CONTEXT_DCHDY.md; visual limits: experiments/yolo/gdt812_additional_page_semantic_bridge/src/VISUAL_LAYOUT_REVIEW.md.

design.mechanism: Two exact written wholes retain distinct participant and relation roles when each crosses local-inscription and running-prose channels on f100v and f77r.
design.unit: The four exact dchdy/soral loci and their complete, independently bounded local prose records on the two already admitted physical folios.
design.contrast: One fixed directed object-use or object-property reading across both folios versus independent register reuse or context-specific senses for either whole.
design.prediction: After singular image owners are independently established, one global assignment of the two complete wholes must preserve participant identity and relation direction in both whole records; an owner mismatch, reversed edge without a written operator, or an incomplete record defeats that assignment.
design.scope: Exploratory source and target binding only; no current score-ready GDT388 packet or meaning claim.
